deep.reconstruction:
This page is §2 of Riemann's Göttingen doctoral dissertation (1851), 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. The previous page (§1, with the footnote criticising Cauchy's Paris Academy note of 31 March 1851) is in the same text. The wording here matches the published §2 essentially verbatim.

The page contains no computation. It sets up the geometric representation that the next page (§3) uses to derive conformality.

(1) Both z and w are variables that can take any complex value. A variable ranging over a connected two-dimensional domain is easier to grasp if it is tied to spatial intuition.

(2) Represent each value z = x + iy by a point O of a plane A with Cartesian coordinates (x, y). Represent each value w = u + iv by a point Q of a plane B with coordinates (u, v). Any dependence of w on z then becomes a dependence of the position of Q on the position of O, i.e. a map F: A -> B, (x, y) -> (u(x, y), v(x, y)).

(3) Suppose each z has a definite w that varies continuously with z, i.e. u and v are continuous functions of x and y. Then:
- every point of A corresponds to a point of B;
- every line 'generally speaking' corresponds to a line;
- every connected piece of surface corresponds to a connected piece of surface.

(4) Hence the dependence of w on z can be pictured as a mapping ('Abbildung') of plane A onto plane B.

This serves §3, which asks what property this mapping has when dw/dz is independent of dz. The answer is local similarity, i.e. conformality.
errors: No real errors. Riemann's hedge 'allgemein zu reden' (generally speaking) is needed: under a merely continuous map a line can degenerate to a point (e.g. a constant map), and a region need not go to a two-dimensional region (e.g. w = x). Read topologically, the statement that the continuous image of a connected set is connected is correct; 'Flächenstück' tacitly assumes non-degeneracy.

'Abbildung der Ebene A auf der Ebene B' is the period idiom (now 'auf die Ebene B'). Strictly, the map need not be surjective, so 'into' rather than 'onto' would be the modern reading. This is not an error in context.

results.what: Representation of a complex function w(z) as a point-to-point mapping of a z-plane onto a w-plane, with the continuity consequences (points to points, curves generically to curves, connected regions to connected regions)
results.modern_name: Geometric (mapping) interpretation of complex functions; continuous image of a connected set is connected
results.usually_credited_to: Plane representation of complex numbers: Wessel (1799), Argand (1806), Gauss (1831). The mapping viewpoint for complex functions: Gauss (conformal mapping, 1822/25) and Riemann (dissertation, 1851)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft or fair copy of §2 of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation, matching the printed text almost word for word. The content is foundational setup, well known and attributed to him.

checkable.asserts: Example of the setup: for w = z^2 the coordinates are u = x^2 - y^2 and v = 2xy, both continuous functions of (x, y). Expected output (0, 0).
The example map satisfies the Cauchy-Riemann equations, i.e. the condition (dw/dz independent of dz) that §3 imposes on the mapping. Expected output (0, 0).

transcription_corrections: The doubtful 'complexen[?]' in line 2 is almost certainly 'complexen', consistent with the published text 'die jeden complexen Werth annehmen können'.
'Abbildung der Ebene A auf der Ebene B' is correctly transcribed, matching the published wording.

Not on this page but relevant: the next-page transcription reads 'die Werthe der Grössen w und z'. Given that x+yi... is listed before u+vi..., the order should be 'z und w', as in the published dissertation. This may be a transcription slip or a slip in the manuscript.
